Title: BUG22 concurrency_cache guiding principle
Code:
```
# Concurrency & Cache — Org Guiding Principle

## TTL Expiry Semantics
- An entry is expired when now >= expires_at (i.e. expires_at <= now), NOT when expires_at < now.
- Return fresh data by calling builder() when entry is absent OR expired.
- Use a monotonic clock (time.monotonic) for TTL calculations, never wall-clock time.

## Stampede Prevention
- Use per-key locking with threading.Event so only one thread calls builder() per cache miss.
- Other threads must wait on the Event and re-read the populated entry rather than calling builder() again.
- On builder() failure, remove the pending entry and signal the Event so waiters don't hang.

## Request Isolation
- Never store per-request state (e.g. request_id) in module-level or class-level variables.
- Use threading.local() or contextvars.ContextVar for per-thread/per-task isolation.
```

Snippet 2: voltsnip/bug22/category/concurrency_cache/oracle_playbook/v2
Title: BUG22 concurrency_cache oracle playbook
Code:
```
# Concurrency cache oracle playbook\n\nRequired outcomes:\n- Coalesce concurrent cache misses per key so builder runs once.\n- Preserve TTL semantics: expired entries should rebuild, not return stale value.\n- Ensure waiters always complete (no self-wait or unresolved event states).\n- Keep synchronization scoped per key to avoid global bottlenecks.\n\nFailure modes to avoid:\n- Multiple builder executions under concurrent misses.\n- Deadlock from waiting on an event that current thread owns.\n- Returning stale entries after expiry.\n- Recursive retries with no progress condition.\n
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any


class TTLCache:
    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = 5.0, time_fn: Callable[[], float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds
        self.time_fn = time_fn or time.monotonic
        self._entries: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

    def get_or_set(self, key: str, builder: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
        now = self.time_fn()
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry is not None and entry["expires_at"] < now:  # BUG_21: inverted — returns stale value after TTL expiry.
            return entry["value"]
        value = builder()  # BUG_22: no synchronization; concurrent misses can stampede.
        self._entries[key] = {"value": value, "expires_at": self.time_fn() + self.ttl_seconds}
        return value
```

retrieved_snippets.code:
# Concurrency cache oracle playbook

Required outcomes:
- Coalesce concurrent cache misses per key so builder runs once.
- Preserve TTL semantics: expired entries should rebuild, not return stale value.
- Ensure waiters always complete (no self-wait or unresolved event states).
- Keep synchronization scoped per key to avoid global bottlenecks.

Failure modes to avoid:
- Multiple builder executions under concurrent misses.
- Deadlock from waiting on an event that current thread owns.
- Returning stale entries after expiry.
- Recursive retries with no progress condition.
